findings.title: GET /pulls/:id no longer refreshes data from GitHub
findings.rationale: Previously, GET /pulls/:id would attempt to fetch the latest files/commits/body from GitHub and persist them, falling back to stored data on failure. The new implementation serves only the stored data without any GitHub call. Any caller that relied on the side effect of refreshing data when viewing a PR will now receive stale data until they explicitly call POST /pulls/:id/refresh. While the PR description documents this change, external callers (e.g., CI, other services) may break. Compatible alternative: keep the old behavior as an opt-in query parameter (e.g., `?refresh=true`) for one release, or document the change prominently in the API changelog.

findings.title: Client-side type mismatch: useRefreshPull expects string but receives number
findings.rationale: The `useRefreshPull` hook is defined with parameter type `prId: string | null | undefined` (client/src/lib/hooks/core.ts line 122), but in PrDetailHeader.tsx it is called with `prId` which is a number (from props `PrDetailHeaderProps`). While the template literal `/pulls/${prId}/refresh` will convert the number to a string at runtime, TypeScript strict mode will flag this as a type error. This could cause build failures or confusion. Fix: change the hook parameter type to accept `number | string | null | undefined` or convert the argument explicitly.

findings.rationale: The old GET handler attempted a live GitHub fetch and persisted the result before returning; if that failed it served from the database. findings.title: useRefreshPull hook does not guard against null/undefined prId
findings.rationale: The mutationFn constructs the URL as `/pulls/${prId}/refresh`. If prId is null or undefined, the request would go to `/pulls/null/refresh` or `/pulls/undefined/refresh`, resulting in a 404. The button in PrDetailHeader guards against this by checking prId before calling mutate, but the hook itself is unsafe if reused elsewhere without a guard.

matched_title: GET /pulls/:id response contract narrowed — live GitHub fields removed

findings.title: GET /pulls/:id response contract narrowed — live GitHub fields removed
findings.rationale: Previously, `GET /pulls/:id` attempted to fetch the latest PR detail from GitHub and, on success, returned the full GitHub response (spread with `id`). On failure, it fell back to the persisted subset. Now it always returns only the persisted subset (id, number, title, author, branch, base, head_sha, additions, deletions, files_count, status, opened_at, updated_at, body, files, commits). Any caller that depended on fields present in the GitHub response but absent from the persisted subset (e.g., `labels`, `milestone`, `draft`, `merged`, `mergeable`, `requested_reviewers`, etc.) will silently lose that data or break. This is a breaking contract change for any deployed caller that does not update in lockstep.

matched_title: New field `reviewUrl` uses camelCase instead of the project's snake_case convention for JSON fields

findings.title: New field `reviewUrl` uses camelCase instead of the project's snake_case convention for JSON fields
findings.rationale: The stack context states that JSON fields are snake_case. All existing fields in `PrMeta` (`cost_usd`, `latest_findings`, etc.) follow this convention. The new field `reviewUrl` breaks that pattern. While existing clients are unaffected (the field is optional), future clients or generic deserializers that expect snake_case may fail or require special handling. The field should be named `review_url` to match the rest of the contract.
